mainTopic: When an עם הארץ is trusted about טהרה: near and in ירושלים, during the רגל, and the purifying of the עזרה afterward
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling about a potter and a חבר at the מודיעים boundary, and אביי proves it from the two halves of a משנה. Next, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about which earthenware vessels an עם הארץ is trusted on, and רבא adds that the liquids inside stay impure. A new משנה says tax collectors and thieves may be believed when they say 'we did not touch.' The גמרא explains this as collectors without a גוי and thieves who did תשובה. In ירושלים people are trusted on even large clay vessels for קודש, because no kilns are built there. During the רגל, all of ישראל count as חברים, based on a פסוק in שופטים. Another משנה argues about finishing wine or dough opened during the רגל, and the גמרא discusses saving it for the next רגל. The amud ends with the purifying of the עזרה vessels after the רגל, and that warning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both leaving counts as outside
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that began on the previous page ends: if the potter and the חבר are both leaving (or both entering) the מודיעים area, it is treated like outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if both of them are leaving, it is treated like outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling from the previous page about where the sale happens. When both people are going the same direction, the sale is treated as if it took place outside the trusted zone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one case gets the 'inside' treatment: the potter is leaving and the חבר is entering, so they can only meet right here. If both are entering, they can wait until they are inside. If both are leaving, they should have done the deal earlier. So in those cases the potter is not trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Like outside, meaning treated as outside the zone where the potter is trusted
Leaving, going out of the area

phrases.english: Or both of them are leaving: it is like outside.
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the potter and the careful buyer. This line finishes a list that started on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ruling begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the potter and the חבר are both leaving (or both entering), the sale is treated as outside the מודיעים, so the potter is not trusted.

steps.title: אביי quotes the משנה and reads the first half
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ruling is already found in a משנה. The משנה trusts a potter who entered inside the מודיעים, which suggests that at the מודיעים itself he is not trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה: 'A potter who sold pots and entered inside the מודיעים is trusted.' The reason is that he is inside the מודיעים. So at the מודיעים itself, he is not trusted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a proof. He quotes a משנה and draws a first inference from its opening words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses 'inside' the מודיעים. אביי reads that stress as meaning that at the boundary line itself the potter is not trusted. This first inference is the setup for the clash that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it, meaning a source already supports this ruling
A town that marks the boundary of the zone around ירושלים
The reason is X, which implies Y, a way of reading an inference out of a text

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned this:
A potter who was selling the pots
and entered inside the Modi'im,
the reason is that he is inside the Modi'im,
so at Modi'im itself, he is not trusted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the ruling in step 1
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between the potter leaving while the חבר enters and both going the same way
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a potter who entered inside the מודיעים

steps.title: The second half of the משנה implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says that if the potter left, he is not trusted. That implies that at the מודיעים itself he is trusted, which clashes with the first inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the end of the משנה: 'If he left, he is not trusted.' So at the מודיעים itself, he is trusted.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside אביי's proof, the גמרא reads the end of the same משנה and gets an inference that contradicts the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half implies the boundary point counts as outside. The second half implies it counts as inside. Both cannot be true in every case, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Now say the last part of the same text

steps.confusionAlert: This contradiction is not an attack on אביי. It is part of his own proof: the only way to fit both halves of the משנה together is the distinction from step 1.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
If he left, he is not trusted.
So at Modi'im itself, he is trusted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the inference drawn in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the first half of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה implies the potter is trusted at the מודיעים itself, while the beginning implies he is not.

steps.title: Two cases explain the two halves
steps.stepSummary: The two halves must be talking about different cases. The second half is a potter leaving while the חבר enters, so he is trusted. The first half is both leaving or both entering, so he is not trusted. That proves the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: So must we not learn from this: here it means a potter leaving and a חבר entering, and there it means both leaving or both entering? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof. The only way to fit both halves of the משנה together is the exact distinction made in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the boundary itself, the potter is trusted only when he is leaving and the חבר is entering, so they cross paths right there. When both go the same way, he is not trusted. The closing 'שמע מינה' confirms that the משנה supports the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from it? This introduces the only way to explain a source
Here ... there, splitting two statements into two different cases
A person who is careful about טהרה laws

steps.whatToRemember: At the מודיעים boundary, the potter is trusted only if he is leaving while the חבר is entering. If both are entering or both are leaving, it counts as outside. אביי proves this from the two halves of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
here, it is a potter leaving and a chaver entering,
phrases.notes: 'Here' points to the end of the משנה, where he is trusted at the boundary.

phrases.english: there, it is where both are leaving
or both are entering.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between steps 2 and 3, which completes the proof of step 1
steps.raayaSupportSource: Fitting together the first and last halves of the משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה supports the distinction: potter leaving and חבר entering counts as inside, and both moving the same way counts as outside.

steps.title: Trusted on small earthenware vessels for קודש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that people are trusted about the purity of small earthenware vessels, even for use with קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: They are trusted about thin, small earthenware vessels, even for קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. A ברייתא gives a rule about which vessels people are trusted on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עם הארץ is not trusted about טהרה. This ברייתא makes an exception for small earthenware vessels, and it applies even to vessels used for holy food. The next steps argue about what counts as 'small.'

phrases.english: A Tanna taught: They are trusted about earthenware vessels
that are small, for sacrificial food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People are trusted about the purity of small earthenware vessels, even for קודש.

steps.title: What counts as a small vessel
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says 'small' means a vessel you can lift with one hand. רבי יוחנן says the rule applies even to vessels you cannot lift with one hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Only if they can be picked up with one hand. רבי יוחנן said: Even if they cannot be picked up with one hand.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how small a vessel has to be for the ברייתא's rule to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש limits the rule to vessels small enough to lift with one hand. רבי יוחנן applies it more widely, to larger vessels too.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when, which adds a condition
Can be picked up with one hand

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Only when they can be picked up with one hand.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even ones that cannot be picked up with one hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְהוּא שֶׁנִּיטָּלִין בְּיָדוֹ אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the word 'small' in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: only vessels that can be lifted with one hand. רבי יוחנן: even larger ones.

steps.title: Empty vessels only, or full ones too
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the trust applies only to empty vessels. רבי יוחנן says it applies even to full ones, and even if the עם הארץ's garment is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The ברייתא taught this only about empty vessels, but not full ones. רבי יוחנן said: Even full ones, and even if his garment is inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The same two אמוראים argue about a second limit on the ברייתא: does it cover vessels that are full of liquid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש keeps the rule narrow and says full vessels are not trusted. רבי יוחנן says the vessel is pure even when full, and even when the עם הארץ's own garment is inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about, which limits a teaching

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only about empty ones,
but full ones, no.
And Rabbi Yochanan said: Even full ones,
and even if his garment is inside it.
phrases.notes: 'His' means the עם הארץ selling the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second argument between the same אמוראים about the scope of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: only empty vessels. רבי יוחנן: even full ones, even with his garment inside.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees the liquids are impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even רבי יוחנן agrees that the liquids inside a full vessel are impure, even though the vessel is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוחנן agrees about the liquids themselves, that they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא limits רבי יוחנן's lenient view: the vessel is pure, but the liquid inside it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's leniency covers only the vessel. The liquid inside is still impure. This creates an odd result, a pure container holding impure liquid, which the next step defends.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
And Rabbi Yochanan agrees about the liquids themselves,
that they are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רבי יוחנן's view from step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי יוחנן, the liquids inside are impure, though the vessel is pure.

steps.title: A jug and its liquid can differ
steps.stepSummary: Do not be surprised. There is a known case where a jug full of liquid is impure with seven-day טומאה, while the liquid inside stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not be surprised, because with a jug full of liquids, the jug is impure with seven-day impurity and the liquids are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the obvious surprise by pointing to another case where a container and what is inside it have different statuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might ask how a pure vessel can hold impure liquid. רבא shows that the law already allows a container and its contents to be split: in the jug case, the jug is impure and the liquid is pure. So the split in רבי יוחנן's case is not strange.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, a small earthenware vessel from an עם הארץ is pure even when full. But the liquid in it is still impure, and that split is not strange, since the law has other cases where a container and its contents differ.

phrases.english: And do not be surprised,
for a jug full of liquids:
the jug is impure with a seven-day impurity,
phrases.notes: Seven-day impurity is the level that comes from contact with a dead body.

phrases.english: and the liquids are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling in step 8 with a parallel case
steps.raayaObject: That a pure vessel can hold impure liquid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a jug that is impure while the liquids inside it are pure

steps.title: Tax collectors and thieves are trusted to say they did not touch
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that גבאין who entered a house, and גנבים who returned vessels, are trusted to say 'we did not touch.' In ירושלים everyone is trusted about קודש, and during the רגל even about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Tax collectors who went into a house, and also thieves who gave back the vessels, are believed when they say: 'We did not touch.' In ירושלים people are believed about holy food, and during the festival they are believed even about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where even an עם הארץ is trusted about טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is normally not trusted about purity. This משנה gives two cases where he is still believed when he says he did not touch the items. It also adds a place-based leniency: in ירושלים for קודש all year, and for תרומה during the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: Tax collectors, here people who are עמי הארץ
The time of a pilgrimage festival
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be kept pure

phrases.english: MISHNA: Tax collectors who entered into the house,
and likewise thieves who returned the vessels —
are trusted to say: We did not touch.
And in Jerusalem they are trusted about holy food,
and at the time of the festival even about teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of earthenware vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבאין who entered a house and גנבים who returned vessels are trusted to say they did not touch; in ירושלים all are trusted about קודש, and during the רגל also about תרומה.

steps.title: Another משנה says the whole house is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in טהרות that says when tax collectors enter a house, the whole house is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a different משנה teaches: tax collectors who entered a house, the whole house is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה with another משנה that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה believes the collectors when they say they touched nothing. The other משנה makes the whole house impure, so it does not believe them at all. Both cannot be true in the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other; a contradiction is raised

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they raised a contradiction:
Tax collectors who entered into the house —
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in טהרות, not our משנה.

phrases.english: the whole house is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the משנה in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that גבאין are trusted to say 'we did not touch.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in טהרות rules the whole house impure when גבאין enter, meaning they are not trusted.

steps.title: It depends on whether a גוי was with them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the משנה in טהרות speaks of collectors with a גוי, while our משנה speaks of collectors without a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. That one is when a גוי is with them; this one is when no גוי is with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by splitting the two משניות into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גוי comes along, the collectors search the whole house, so the whole house is impure. When no גוי is there, they can be believed that they touched nothing. So each משנה is talking about a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; here is the answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
that is where there is a gentile with them,
phrases.notes: 'That' is the משנה in טהרות, where the whole house is impure.

phrases.english: this is where there is no gentile with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּאִיכָּא גּוֹי בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות talk about the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טהרות case has a גוי with the collectors; our משנה has no גוי.

steps.title: A משנה shows the role of the גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if a גוי is with them, they are believed to say 'we did not enter,' but not 'we entered but did not touch.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If a גוי is with them, they are believed to say 'we did not enter,' but they are not believed to say 'we entered but did not touch.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a משנה that already makes this exact distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source shows that having a גוי along changes the law. With a גוי, once they admit they went in, we assume they touched everything. They are only believed if they say they never went in at all.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned: If there is a gentile with them —
they are trusted to say 'We did not enter,'
but they are not trusted to say
'We entered but did not touch.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 12 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the presence of a גוי is what makes the collectors untrustworthy about not touching.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (טהרות): with a גוי present they are believed only to say 'we did not enter.'
steps.whatToRemember: Tax collectors alone are believed when they say 'we did not touch.' With a גוי along, they are only believed if they say 'we did not enter at all.'

steps.title: Why does the גוי make a difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why having a גוי with them changes anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when a גוי is with them, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is clear, but the logic is not. Why should someone else's presence make the collectors touch everything? The next step gives two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: And when there is a gentile with them,
what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִיכָּא גּוֹי בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the distinction in steps 12 and 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the presence of a גוי makes the collectors search and touch the whole house.

steps.title: Fear of the גוי or fear of the government
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר answer differently: one says they fear the גוי himself, the other says they fear the מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר: One said, they are afraid of the גוי. The other said, they are afraid of the government.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two reasons why the collectors search everything when a גוי is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view: the גוי is their boss, and they fear he will punish them. The other view: they fear the גוי will report them to the מלכות if they do not search well. Either way, they touch everything.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar:
One said: The fear of the gentile is upon them.
And one said: The fear of the government is upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either fear of the גוי himself, or fear that the מלכות will hear about it, pushes them to search everything.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the two reasons would lead to different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons usually give the same result. The גמרא wants a case where the two views would actually disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the dispute in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where fear of the גוי and fear of the מלכות give different results.

steps.title: A גוי who is not important
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a גוי who is not important: they do not fear him, but he could still report them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a גוי who is not important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two views split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי has no power, the collectors are not afraid of him himself. So by the 'fear of the גוי' view, they could be believed. But he can still report them, so by the 'fear of the מלכות' view, they are still not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: A גוי who is not important, with no authority

phrases.english: The difference between them is
a gentile who is not important.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גוי without authority: no fear of him personally, but there is still fear of the מלכות.

steps.title: Thieves make impure only where they walked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line about thieves and challenges it with a משנה that says thieves make impure the places they walked.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And likewise thieves who returned the vessels.' But a different משנה teaches: thieves who entered a house, only the place where their feet stepped is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case of our משנה, the thieves, and raises a contradiction from טהרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה believes thieves who say 'we did not touch.' The other משנה makes impure every place they walked, without believing them. So the two seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the feet stepped

phrases.english: And likewise thieves who returned the vessels.
And they raised a contradiction: Thieves who entered into the house —
nothing is impure except
the place where the feet of the thieves stepped.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הַגַּנָּבִים שֶׁהֶחְזִירוּ אֶת הַכֵּלִים. וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tax collectors and turns to the thieves in the משנה of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that thieves who returned vessels are trusted to say 'we did not touch.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in טהרות makes the area where thieves walked impure, so they are not trusted to say they did not touch.

steps.title: Our משנה speaks of thieves who did תשובה
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס in the name of רב answers that our משנה speaks of thieves who did תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס said in the name of רב: It is when they did תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction about thieves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thieves who did תשובה are now trusted, so we believe them that they did not touch. The משנה in טהרות speaks of thieves who did not do תשובה.

phrases.english: Rav Pinḥas said in the name of Rav:
When they repented.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פִּנְחָס מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: כְּשֶׁעָשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות talk about the same kind of thief.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה speaks of thieves who did תשובה; the טהרות משנה speaks of thieves who did not.

steps.title: The wording 'returned the vessels' proves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the משנה's wording supports רב: 'returned the vessels' shows they repented. The גמרא concludes this is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too, since it says: 'who returned the vessels.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב's answer from the exact words of the משנה and closes the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not just say 'thieves'; it says thieves 'who returned the vessels.' Giving back what they stole on their own shows they did תשובה. So רב's answer fits the משנה, and the גמרא accepts it.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is exact too; it also fits
Learn from this; it is proven

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
who returned the vessels.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 19 from the wording of the משנה in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה speaks of thieves who did תשובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'שהחזירו את הכלים' (who returned the vessels).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Thieves who did תשובה and returned what they stole are trusted to say they did not touch; other thieves are not.
steps.whatToRemember: Tax collectors are trusted when no גוי is with them. Thieves are trusted when they did תשובה, which is shown by their returning the vessels.

steps.title: In ירושלים, even large clay vessels are trusted for קודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that in ירושלים people are trusted on קודש, and brings a ברייתא adding that this includes large clay vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: in ירושלים they are trusted regarding קודש. A ברייתא taught: they are trusted even about large clay vessels used for קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and adds a ברייתא that widens it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עם הארץ is not trusted to say his clay vessels are pure. The משנה says that in ירושלים he is trusted for קודש. The ברייתא adds that this is true even for big, heavy clay vessels, not only small ones.

keyTerms.meaning: They are believed or trusted (here, about purity)
Sacred food, such as meat from קרבנות

phrases.english: And in Jerusalem they are believed regarding sacred food.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. "They" means עמי הארץ, people not careful about purity.

phrases.english: A tanna taught: they are believed
even regarding large earthenware vessels for sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: נֶאֱמָנִין עַל כְּלֵי חֶרֶס גַּסִּין לַקּוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion about thieves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ירושלים, עמי הארץ are trusted about the purity of even large clay vessels used for קודש.

steps.title: Why such a big leniency?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן were so lenient about clay vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this leniency?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן went so far in trusting people about clay vessels. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן were usually strict about עמי הארץ and purity. So a leniency this wide needs a reason, and the גמרא asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And why so much? (asking for the reason behind a big leniency)

phrases.english: And why all this much?
phrases.notes: He means: why were the רבנן so lenient here, when they are normally strict?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the leniency taught in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רבנן were so lenient about clay vessels in ירושלים.

steps.title: Because no kilns are made in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Kilns are not allowed in ירושלים, so clay vessels must come from outside the city. That is why the רבנן were lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because kilns are not made in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: you cannot make clay pots in ירושלים, so the רבנן had to be lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pottery is fired in a kiln, and kilns are not built in ירושלים. All clay vessels therefore come from outside the city, often from עמי הארץ. Without this leniency, people would not have enough pure vessels for קודש.
steps.whatToRemember: In ירושלים, עמי הארץ are trusted even on large clay vessels for קודש, because no kilns may be built in the city and all pots must be brought in from outside.

phrases.english: Because kilns are not made in Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Clay vessels cannot be made in ירושלים, so they must be brought from outside, and the רבנן had to be lenient.

steps.title: Where do we learn that during the Festival even תרומה is trusted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that during the רגל people are trusted even on תרומה, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: during the רגל they are trusted even about תרומה. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks what source it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All year, עמי הארץ are not trusted about the purity of תרומה. The משנה says the רגל is different. The גמרא wants a source for why the time of the רגל changes the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of the pilgrimage Festival
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be eaten in purity
From where are these words learned?

phrases.english: And during the time of the Festival
even regarding teruma.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for trusting עמי הארץ on תרומה during the רגל.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the פסוק makes all of ישראל חברים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי brings a פסוק showing that when all of ישראל gather together, they all count as חברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the פסוק says "And all the men of ישראל gathered to the city, as one man, חברים." The פסוק made all of them חברים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the source. A פסוק calls all of ישראל, gathered together, "חברים."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר is someone trusted on purity. The פסוק describes the whole nation gathered in one place and calls them "חברים." So when everyone gathers, as they do on the רגל, everyone gets the trusted status of a חבר, even for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: people trusted to be careful about purity
The פסוק made them (treats them as)

steps.whatToRemember: During the רגל, when all of ישראל gather, everyone counts as a חבר, so even עמי הארץ are trusted about תרומה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
For the verse says:
"And all the men of Israel gathered to the city
as one man, united (chaverim)"
The verse made them all chaverim.
phrases.notes: A חבר is someone trusted to keep purity, so the פסוק gives everyone that trust.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in שופטים calls all of ישראל, gathered together, חברים. So during the רגל, everyone has the trusted status of a חבר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the rules of purity change during the רגל, which is the background for the next משנה about selling wine and dough.

steps.title: New משנה: finishing a barrel or dough opened during the Festival
steps.stepSummary: Someone opened his wine barrel or started selling his dough during the רגל. רבי יהודה says he may finish it, and the חכמים say he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who opens his barrel, or starts on his dough, during the רגל: רבי יהודה says he may finish it. The חכמים say he may not finish it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks what happens after the רגל to wine or dough that was opened during it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the רגל, עמי הארץ touched the wine or dough, and their touch counted as pure. After the רגל, they no longer have the status of חברים. רבי יהודה says the seller may keep selling it as pure. The חכמים say he may not.

keyTerms.meaning: During the time of the רגל

steps.confusionAlert: The argument is about what happens AFTER the רגל ends. During the רגל itself, everyone agrees the food counts as pure.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who opens his barrel,
and one who begins on his dough
during the time of the Festival,
Rabbi Yehuda says: he may finish it,
and the Rabbis say: he may not finish it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפּוֹתֵחַ אֶת חָבִיתוֹ, וְהַמַּתְחִיל בְּעִיסָּתוֹ עַל גַּב הָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that builds on the idea that everyone is trusted during the רגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: wine or dough opened during the רגל may be finished in purity afterward. חכמים: it may not.

steps.title: May he save the barrel for the next Festival?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא sat together, and one asked whether the seller may put the barrel aside until the next רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא were sitting in the courtyard of רבי יצחק נפחא. One of them began and said: may he leave it for another רגל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of two אמוראים sitting together, and one asks a new question about the משנה. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, he may not finish the barrel after the רגל. The question is whether he may set it aside and sell it at the next רגל, when everyone is trusted again.

keyTerms.meaning: One of them began and said

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha were sitting
in the courtyard of Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha.
One of them opened and said:
What is the law about leaving it for another Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּתַח חַד וַאֲמַר: מַהוּ שֶׁיַּנִּיחֶנָּה לְרֶגֶל אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה with a follow-up question about the view of the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a barrel opened during one רגל may be saved and sold in purity at the next רגל.

steps.title: The other sage says the barrel cannot be saved for the next festival
steps.stepSummary: The second sage rejects the idea: everyone has already touched the barrel, so how can it be saved for another רגל?
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one said to him: Everyone's hand has been touching it, and you are suggesting he may leave it for another רגל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The other sage answers the question from the last step with a strong 'no.' Lots of people touched the barrel during the רגל, so it cannot be kept pure until the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the רגל, every kind of person, including an עם הארץ, handled this wine. This sage assumes all that touching left its mark. So saving the barrel for the next רגל makes no sense to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He may set it aside, leave it

phrases.english: The other one said to him:
Everyone's hand has been touching it,
and you say he may leave it for another festival?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִידַּךְ: יַד הַכֹּל מְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The barrel was touched by everyone, so it cannot be saved for the next רגל.

steps.title: The first sage pushes back: people touched it all festival long
steps.stepSummary: The first sage challenges this: people were touching it during the whole רגל too, and that was fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is that to say that until now, everyone's hand was not touching it?
steps.whatsHappening: The first sage pushes back. People touched the barrel all through the רגל and it stayed usable, so why should that touching matter now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that the touching already happened during the רגל, when it did not make the wine impure. If that touching did not count then, why should it count later? Nobody new has touched the barrel since.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a word that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: He said to him: Is that to say that until now
everyone's hand was not touching it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone's touching makes the barrel unfit for the next רגל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same touching happened during the רגל and the wine was still allowed, so the touching itself should not be a problem.

steps.title: The festival made the touching pure, but only while it lasted
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תורה treats an עם הארץ as pure only during the רגל. Once the רגל is over, that same touching counts as impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare the two? Granted, until now the Merciful One declared the impurity of an עם הארץ pure during the רגל. But now, after the רגל, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The second sage answers the challenge. The touching was only treated as pure because it was the רגל. Now that the רגל is over, it is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this sage's view, the purity of the עם הארץ's touch was a special rule for the רגל time, not a permanent one. Once the רגל ends, the touching that already happened counts as normal impurity, so the barrel cannot be saved for the next רגל. The גמרא does not stop here. Steps 31–34 bring ברייתות on this same question.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is not careful about purity laws
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the עם הארץ's touch was never impure. It was impure, but the תורה ignored that impurity only during the רגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the purity of the רגל is a time-limited rule. It explains why things touched during the רגל go back to being impure afterward.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can you compare?!
Granted, until now,
the impurity of an עם הארץ during the festival
the Merciful One declared pure,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the פסוק from step 25, that when all ישראל gather they all count as חברים.

phrases.english: but now it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Touching that did not matter during the רגל should not matter later either.
steps.terutzMaskana: The purity of the רגל lasts only during the רגל. Afterward, the same touching counts as impure.

steps.title: Two ברייתות seem to argue about the same question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this argument between אמוראים matches an earlier argument between תנאים, since one ברייתא says he may save the barrel and another says he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like an argument between תנאים. One ברייתא teaches: he may leave it for another רגל. Another ברייתא teaches: he may not leave it for another רגל. Isn't this an argument between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the same argument already appears among the תנאים. Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on saving the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two ברייתות disagree, it seems that two תנאים argued about this question. Then the two אמוראים would simply be following different תנאים. The next step will test this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (a suggestion that may be rejected)
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tannaim,
for one teaches: He may leave it for another festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: לֹא יַנִּיחֶנָּה לְרֶגֶל אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and another teaches: He may not leave it for another festival.
Is it not a dispute of tannaim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the אמוראים' argument in earlier sources.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between the אמוראים the same as an argument between תנאים?

steps.title: No, the ברייתות follow רבי יהודה and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The ברייתא that allows saving the barrel follows רבי יהודה, and the one that forbids it follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא that says 'he may leave it' follows רבי יהודה, and the one that says 'he may not leave it' follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the two ברייתות do not need to be a new argument. They simply follow the two sides of the argument already in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 already showed that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about this seller. So each ברייתא can be matched to one side of that known argument. These are not two new תנאים arguing about saving the barrel.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, הָא דְּקָתָנֵי יַנִּיחֶנָּה — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: No, this one that teaches 'he may leave it' is Rabbi Yehuda,
and that one that teaches 'he may not leave it' is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתות are a new argument between תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות can be explained as following רבי יהודה and the רבנן of the משנה.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה lets him finish the barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this matching: רבי יהודה allows the seller to finish the barrel, so why would he talk about saving it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think so? Doesn't רבי יהודה say he may finish it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the matching it just made. It does not make sense for רבי יהודה to be the one who talks about saving the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets the seller finish selling right away, after the רגל. Someone who may finish selling now has no reason to wait for the next רגל. So the 'he may leave it' ברייתא does not fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so?

phrases.english: And do you really think so?
Rabbi Yehuda says he may finish it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, יִגְמוֹר קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the matching made in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: Matching the 'he may leave it' ברייתא to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה allows finishing the barrel right away, so saving it for the next רגל would be pointless for him.

steps.title: Switch the matching: 'he may not leave it' means he doesn't need to
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the matching. 'He may not leave it' is רבי יהודה, meaning he does not need to save it because he may finish it now. 'He may leave it' is the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: The ברייתא that teaches 'he may not leave it' follows רבי יהודה, and the one that teaches 'he may leave it' follows the רבנן. And what does 'he may not leave it' mean? That he does not need to leave it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by switching which ברייתא goes with which opinion. It also reads 'he may not leave it' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the seller may finish the barrel now, so he does not need to save it. That is what 'he may not leave it' means. For the רבנן, he may not finish it now, but he may save it for the next רגל. The two ברייתות are still not a new argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: That he does not need to

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'he may not leave it' does not mean saving it is forbidden. It means there is no need to save it.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות fit the משנה's argument. רבי יהודה: finish it now, no need to save it. רבנן: don't finish it now, but you may save it for the next רגל.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הָא דְּקָתָנֵי לֹא יַנִּיחֶנָּה — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rather: this one that teaches 'he may not leave it' is Rabbi Yehuda,
and that one that teaches 'he may leave it' is the Rabbis.
And what does 'he may not leave it' mean?
That he does not need to leave it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָא דְּקָתָנֵי לֹא יַנִּיחֶנָּה — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 by switching the matching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching which ברייתא matches which opinion, and reading 'not' as 'no need'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He may leave it' follows רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'He may not leave it' follows רבי יהודה, meaning there is no need to save it. 'He may leave it' follows the רבנן.

steps.title: After the festival, the Temple courtyard is purified
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: once the רגל has passed, the כהנים purify the vessels of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Once the רגל has passed, they put the עזרה through purification.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. After the רגל, the vessels in the עזרה must be purified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the רגל, the touch of an עם הארץ counted as pure. Once it ends, everything touched counts as impure again, as step 30 explained. So the עזרה's vessels need to be purified.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA: Once the festival has passed,
they put the Temple courtyard through purification.
phrases.notes: Literally 'pass over.' Here it means purifying the courtyard's vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the רגל, the vessels of the עזרה are purified.

steps.title: Not on Friday, out of respect for שבת
steps.stepSummary: If the רגל ended so that the next day is Friday, they did not purify that day, out of respect for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the רגל passed into Friday, they would not purify, because of the honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to the rule. If the day after the רגל is Friday, the purification waits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purifying all the vessels takes time and effort. On Friday, the כהנים need that time to get ready for שבת. So the purifying is held off.

phrases.english: If the festival passed into Friday,
they would not purify,
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule of step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No purification on Friday, out of respect for שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: not even on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says they do not purify even on Thursday, because the כהנים are busy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Not even on Thursday, because the כהנים are not free.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds Thursday to the exception. The כהנים are not free to purify then either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא held off only on Friday. רבי יהודה says that on Thursday, too, the כהנים are too busy for this work. The משנה does not say what keeps them busy; the next step explains.
steps.whatToRemember: After the רגל the עזרה is purified, but not on Friday. According to רבי יהודה, not on Thursday either.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא בְּיוֹם חֲמִישִׁי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Not even on Thursday,
because the priests are not free.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא בְּיוֹם חֲמִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the exception of step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, there is no purification on Thursday either, because the כהנים are not free.

steps.title: Why the כהנים are busy on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains רבי יהודה: the כהנים cannot purify the vessels on Thursday because they are busy removing the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: because the כהנים are not free, since they are busy removing the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יהודה meant in the משנה when he said the כהנים are busy. They are busy taking out the ashes from the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 37, רבי יהודה said there is no purifying on Thursday either because the כהנים are not free. This ברייתא fills in the missing detail of what keeps them busy: removing the ashes. So the purifying has to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught. This introduces a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה.
The ashes from the offerings burned on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יהודה's delay is a practical one. The כהנים simply have no time, and nothing about the purifying itself is the problem.

phrases.english: גמרא: It was taught:
because the כהנים are not free
from removing the ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason רבי יהודה gave in step 37 (the כהנים are busy).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Thursday the כהנים are busy removing the ashes, so they do not purify the vessels.

steps.title: How are the עזרה vessels purified?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens by asking how the vessels of the עזרה are purified after the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How do they carry out the purifying of the עזרה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a question. It is setting up an explanation of the actual steps for purifying the vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 said the כהנים purify the vessels after the רגל, but it did not say how. This question opens the step-by-step answer that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, meaning 'our משנה'. A new משנה starts here.
They carry out, they put through a process
The purifying of the Temple courtyard and its vessels

phrases.english: משנה: How do they carry out
the purifying of the עזרה?
phrases.notes: This means the vessels in the עזרה, which the כהנים purify after the רגל, as in step 35.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that explains the purifying mentioned in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical procedure for purifying the vessels of the עזרה after the רגל.

steps.title: Immersing the vessels and warning the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה answers: they immerse the vessels that were in the מקדש, and they tell the כהנים to be careful. The warning continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They immerse the vessels that were in the מקדש, and they say to them: Be careful...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts answering its question. The vessels are immersed in a מקוה, and the כהנים receive a warning that is completed in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing the vessels is the basic way to purify them. The משנה also begins a warning to the כהנים, but the sentence is cut off here, so we do not yet know what they must be careful about.

keyTerms.meaning: They immerse in a מקוה to make something טהור

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops at 'Be careful'. Do not guess what the warning is. The משנה finishes it on the next amud.

phrases.english: They immerse the vessels
that were in the מקדש,
and they say to them: Be careful
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the כהנים. The rest of the warning comes in the next line of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The vessels of the מקדש are immersed, and the כהנים are warned to be careful. The details of the warning follow in the next part.
